title: Cap. VI Arg. 9: one ratio of predestination — Head and members alike
latin: Unica est ratio praedestinationis tum quoad Caput et membra, tum quoad membra inter se collata. Hoc est: Si praedestinatio Christi ad officium Mediatoris et Salvatoris fuerit gratuita, et non ex praevisione meritorum, tum multo magis praedestinatio nostri ad beneficium salutis gratuita esse debet. Porro, Si manifestum sit quaedam Christi membra ad vitam aeternam absque ullo respectu ad praevisae fidei aut perseverantiae conditionem fuisse praedestinata, tum idem statuendum est de reliquis omnibus. Praedestinationem enim, quoad conditiones praerequisitas aut non praerequisitas, uniformem esse, extra dubium est.
pass_a: There is one ratio of predestination both as regards the Head and the members, and as regards the members compared among themselves. That is: If the predestination of Christ to the office of Mediator and Savior was gratuitous, and not from foresight of merits, then much more ought our predestination to the benefit of salvation to be gratuitous. Further, If it is manifest that certain members of Christ were predestinated to eternal life without any respect to the condition of foresighted faith or perseverance, then the same is to be established concerning all the rest. For that predestination, as regards conditions presupposed or not presupposed, is uniform, is beyond doubt.
pass_b: One ratio of predestination — Head and members, and members among themselves. If Christ's predestination to Mediator and Savior was gratuitous, not from foresight of merits, then much more must ours to the benefit of salvation be gratuitous. And if some of Christ's members were clearly predestined to eternal life with no regard to foresighted faith or perseverance, the same holds for all the rest. Predestination is uniform as to whether conditions are presupposed or not — that is beyond doubt.

title: Cap. VI Arg. 9: first — Christ the Mediator predestined without prior merits (Augustine)
latin: Quod ad prius: Si quaeratur, Quomodo Christus in Salvatorem praedestinatus? secundum Dei gratuitum beneplacitum, an secundum praevisionem operum? audite eundem Augustinum: Est etiam praeclarissimum lumen praedestinationis et gratiae ipse Salvator, ipse Mediator Dei et hominum, homo Christus Jesus: qui ut hoc esset, quibus tandem suis, vel operum vel fidei, praecedentibus meritis naturae humanae quae in illo est comparavit? De Praed. Sanct. cap. 15.
pass_a: As to the former: If it be asked, How was Christ predestinated to be Savior? according to the gratuitous good pleasure of God, or according to foresight of works? hear the same Augustine: There is also a most illustrious light of predestination and grace, the Savior himself, the Mediator of God and men, the man Christ Jesus: who, that he might be this, by what preceding merits of his own, whether of works or of faith, did the human nature which is in him procure it? On the Predestination of the Saints, chapter 15.
pass_b: First limb: how was Christ predestined Savior — by God's gratuitous good pleasure, or by foresight of works? Hear Augustine (On the Predestination of the Saints 15): the brightest light of predestination and grace is the Savior himself, the Mediator, the man Christ Jesus — and by what prior merits of his own, of works or of faith, did the human nature in him earn to be that?

lemmas.gloss: Augustine: no prior merits in Christ's humanity

title: Cap. VI Arg. 9: second — infant elect without foresight faith; Augustine vs Pelagians
latin: Jam quod ad posterius, nempe conformitatem praedestinationis inter ipsa membra: clarum est multa membra Christi in vitam aeternam fuisse praedestinata absque antecedaneo intuitu fidei aut perseverantiae in eadem. Nam cum fides perseverans non consideretur nisi in illis qui utuntur ratione et libero arbitrio, quotquot in infantia morientes salvantur, absque hujus intuitu ad salutem fuisse destinatos est necesse. At multi ea aetate moriuntur, de quorum salute Ecclesia nunquam dubitavit. Multi ergo et electi et servati fuerunt, in quibus haec praevisio fidei et perseverantiae locum habere non potuit. Hoc argumento ab infantibus electis petito Augustinus passim occludit ora Pelagianorum, qui ex praevisis meritis praedestinationem ad vitam statuerunt: De praed. et grat. cap. 7; De bono persever. cap. 8 et 12; De peccat. mer. et remiss. lib. 1. cap. 21; Contr. 2 Epist. Pelag. lib. 2. cap. 7.
pass_a: Now as to the latter, namely the conformity of predestination among the members themselves: it is clear that many members of Christ were predestinated unto eternal life without an antecedent intuition of faith or perseverance in the same. For since persevering faith is not considered except in those who use reason and free choice, as many as dying in infancy are saved, it is necessary that they were destined to salvation without this intuition. But many die at that age, of whose salvation the Church never doubted. Many therefore both were elected and saved, in whom this foresight of faith and perseverance could have no place. By this argument drawn from elect infants Augustine everywhere shuts the mouths of the Pelagians, who established predestination to life from foresighted merits: On Predestination and Grace ch. 7; On the Gift of Perseverance ch. 8 and 12; On the Merits and Remission of Sins book 1 ch. 21; Against Two Letters of the Pelagians book 2 ch. 7.
pass_b: Second limb — conformity among the members: many of Christ's members were predestined to eternal life with no prior regard to faith or perseverance. Persevering faith is only considered in those who use reason and free choice; so all who die in infancy and are saved must have been destined to salvation without that regard. Many die at that age whose salvation the Church never doubted. Many, then, were both elect and saved in whom foresight of faith and perseverance could have no place. By elect infants Augustine everywhere stops the Pelagians' mouths — those who grounded predestination to life in foresighted merits (On Predestination and Grace 7; On the Gift of Perseverance 8, 12; On Merits and Remission 1.21; Against Two Letters of the Pelagians 2.7).

lemmas.gloss: infants dying saved without foresight faith

title: Cap. VI Arg. 9: Prosper on infants; Grevinchovius — if eternal life, then election
latin: Cui suffragatur Prosper in lib. De libero arbitrio: In infantibus nec praecedens eligitur nec secutura devotio. De his loquor qui mox ut nati sunt renascuntur, et rapti ab hac vita aeternae beatitudini deputantur. Grevinchovius in Disputatione de Electione ex fide praevisa, pag. 143, hoc argumento irretitus, eo tandem delabitur, ut in dubium vocet utrum sit ulla infantium electio necne. Sed quorum est vita aeterna, illorum proculdubio est electio ad vitam aeternam, cum numerus glorificatorum numerum praedestinatorum sive electorum non excedat. Nam quos praedestinavit glorificavit, et non alios, ut recte Augustinus illum locum Apostoli exposuit. Sic sanus Prosper: Non alii venient in consortium haereditatis Christi, quam qui ante constitutionem mundi electi sunt, et praedestinati atque praesciti secundum propositum ejus, qui omnia operatur secundum consilium voluntatis suae. Si ergo quidam infantes haereditate caelesti donantur, iidem etiam praedestinantur sive eliguntur.
pass_a: To which Prosper assents in the book On Free Choice: In infants neither preceding nor following devotion is elected. I speak of those who as soon as they are born are reborn, and snatched from this life are assigned to eternal beatitude. Grevinchovius in the Disputation on Election from foresighted faith, p. 143, entangled by this argument, at last slips so far as to call into doubt whether there is any election of infants or not. But of those whose is eternal life, of them without doubt is election to eternal life, since the number of the glorified does not exceed the number of the predestinated or elect. For whom he predestinated, them he glorified, and not others, as Augustine rightly expounded that place of the Apostle. So sound Prosper: No others will come into the fellowship of the inheritance of Christ than those who before the foundation of the world were elected, and predestinated and foreknown according to the purpose of him who works all things according to the counsel of his will. If therefore certain infants are gifted with the heavenly inheritance, the same also are predestinated or elected.
pass_b: Prosper agrees (On Free Choice): in infants neither prior nor later devotion is chosen — he means those reborn as soon as born, and snatched from this life into eternal beatitude. Grevinchovius (Disputation on Election from foresighted faith, p. 143), caught by this, finally doubts whether there is any infant election at all. But whoever has eternal life surely has election to eternal life — the glorified do not outnumber the predestined. Whom he predestined, them he glorified, and no others (so Augustine on the Apostle). Sound Prosper: none enter Christ's inheritance but those elected before the world's foundation, predestined and foreknown according to his purpose. If some infants receive the heavenly inheritance, those same are predestined or elect.

title: Cap. VI Arg. 9 close: Christ and Christian infants not from foresight — nor the rest
latin: Sed Grevinchovius fortasse id voluit, omnes infantes salvari promiscue, ac proinde nullam esse electionem infantium. Sed huic uni malesano disputatori oppono catholicae Ecclesiae judicium, quae semper sensit omnes infantes nasci filios irae, renasci autem non omnes, sed illos solos quos Deus indebita gratia dignatur. Summa est: Christus non est praedestinatus ex aliqua praevisione meritorum; neque infantes Christianorum: Ergo nec reliqui Christiani, quorum omnium electio est uniusmodi et ejusdem rationis cum electione sui Capitis, et inter se.
pass_a: But Grevinchovius perhaps meant this, that all infants are saved indiscriminately, and therefore that there is no election of infants. But against this one unsound disputant I set the judgment of the catholic Church, which always felt that all infants are born children of wrath, but that not all are reborn, but those alone whom God dignifies with unowed grace. The sum is: Christ is not predestinated from any foresight of merits; nor the infants of Christians: Therefore neither the remaining Christians, of all of whom the election is of one kind and of the same ratio with the election of their Head, and among themselves.
pass_b: Or Grevinchovius meant all infants are saved alike, so there is no infant election. Against that one unsound disputant stands the catholic Church's judgment: all infants are born children of wrath; not all are reborn — only those God dignifies with unowed grace. Sum: Christ is not predestined from foresight of merits; nor Christian infants. Therefore neither are the remaining Christians — whose election is of one kind and the same ratio with their Head's, and among themselves.
